_note: victor_e0n_multitask_nathan_recipe (E0-N, recipe check): E0 (victor_e0_multitask_convnext) moved to the training settings of Nathan's Nat_multitask_convnext_base (test HM 65.8 in docs/all_results.csv, vs E0's 62.9), run through the same trainer (train/train_cnn.py) and GPU as E0, so the two differ only in recipe. Question: is Nathan's recipe better on validation? If E0-N beats E0's mean validation HM (58.9) by about 2-3 points or more, E1 and later runs move to this recipe (E1-N first); otherwise the ladder stays on Hein's recipe. Not copied from his trainer: early stopping (this run trains all 20 epochs per split and picks the epoch on validation, as E0) and physical batch 32 (16 x 2 accumulation here, equivalent with LayerNorm).

data._note: Same splits and 333-pair protocol as the CLIP versions (generalised zero-shot).

model._note: Nathan's settings: head dropout 0.3 (E0: 0.2), no stochastic depth (E0: 0.1). LayerNorm, so 16 x 2 accumulation equals his batch 32.

input._note: As E0 but bilinear resampling (Nathan's trainer default; E0 uses bicubic).

augmentation._note: Nathan's settings: random resized crop scale 0.25-1 (E0: 0.5-1); flips and colour jitter as E0.

loss._note: Cross-entropy with label smoothing 0.1 (long-tailed, noisy labels: median 7 images per pair). For the multi-task model the two head losses are summed with equal weight.

optimizer._note: AdamW, Nathan's learning rates: backbone 1e-4, heads 1e-3 (twice E0's); weight decay 0.05 as E0.

validation._note: Same validation procedure, splits and gamma grid (log-probability units) as aniq_baseline_independent_cnn; 3 splits (Hein's study used one), so epoch and gamma are chosen the same way as for every other baseline.

training._note: Nathan's schedule: no warmup, plain cosine to 0 over each run's own length (train_cnn.py's default without the recipe keys; his refit_schedule 'compress'), no gradient clipping. Physical batch 16 x 2 accumulation = effective 32. max_epochs 20 as E0 and Nathan.

evaluation._note: Pair score = log P(crop) + log P(disease). gamma (subtracted from seen pairs) from validation, in log-probability units.

runtime._note: 2 dataloader workers (4 ran out of RAM on the 16 GB laptop: train and validation loaders each keep their workers alive); images come from the resized cache.
